set -euxo pipefail

[[ -f $1 ]] || { echo "no such file: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
log_file=$(printf %s "$1" | openssl dgst -sha256 -r | cut -d' ' -f1).log

llama-bench -m $* -ngl 99 -n 0 -p 4096 -d 262144 --verbose --no-warmup -r 1 2>&1 >$log_file
rg '^load_tensors:.*model buffer size' $log_file

content.text:
Shell redirections are processed **left to right**:

```bash
2>&1 >"$log_file"
```

This does:

1. Point stderr (`2`) at the current stdout—the terminal.
2. Redirect stdout (`1`) to the log file.

So stderr remains on the terminal. Reverse the order:

```bash
llama-bench -m "$@" -ngl 99 -n 0 -p 4096 -d 262144 \
  --verbose --no-warmup -r 1 >"$log_file" 2>&1
```

Now stdout is redirected first, then stderr is pointed at that redirected stdout.

Also, prefer `"$@"` over unquoted `$*`; it preserves argument boundaries. If you want output both displayed and logged:

```bash
llama-bench ... 2>&1 | tee "$log_file"
```
